display_long_description:
VECTOR ROCKS
 
No textures. No color palette. Just bright white vector lines on infinite black, and a sphere of space that
surrounds you completely.
 
 You stand at the center of the playfield. Your ship flies across its inner surface, around you, over your head and
down behind your back. There are no screen edges to wrap around: the sphere is the wrap. Turn your head to follow
 the action; when your ship slips out of view, a marker at the edge of your vision points the way.

SIMPLE, ON PURPOSE
Every shape is drawn on a single grid: the triangle you fly, the faceted rocks, even the lettering. The only color
 in the game comes from the lens itself. Look toward the edge of your vision and every line splits into a faint
rainbow fringe, like light through glass.
 
 A FIELD THAT FIGHTS ITSELF
 Shoot a rock and it splits into smaller pieces; keep shooting until it's dust. But the rocks don't wait for you.
They drift into each other and crumble on their own, and you hear each crash from exactly where it happens around
you.

AN ORIGINAL SCORE
A sparse, twelve-tone pulse plays one note at a time, never a chord. The longer a wave drags on, the faster it
 beats.
  
 FEATURES
 • 360° spherical playfield, built for VR
 • Pure vector graphics with real-time lens fringing
 • Rocks collide and crumble with directional crash sounds
 • Original generative twelve-tone score
 • Classic arcade rules.
